news.title: No major World Cup regrets, says Tony Popovic, despite shootout heartbreak
news.lede: In his first appearance in front of the media since the last-32 defeat to Egypt the coach, whose tactics elicited some criticism, insists he would not have done anything different. More than two months have passed since Australia’s painful penalty shootout defeat against Egypt ended a World Cup adventure that had begun so brightly. Although the Socceroos upset Turkey and progressed to the knockout stage with the youngest team in the tournament, coach Tony Popovic wore criticism for his selections, especially in that shootout in Dallas. Sitting in front of a bank of microphones in Sydney on Tuesday in his first media appearance since the World Cup, the coach is finally ready to talk.

news.title: New Zealand edge closer to berth at next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand have moved to within one win of qualifying to represent Oceania at next year’s FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. A 6-0 win against Vanuatu at the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa has earned New Zealand a semi-final against New Caledonia, and the winner of that match on Friday will go to the World Cup. The other qualifying team will come from Friday’s other semi-final, between Solomon Islands and Tahiti. Main photo: New Zealand … big win against Vanuatu.

news.title: France face Morocco in high-stakes World Cup quarter-final tomorrow
news.lede: A place in the FIFA World Cup 2026 semi-finals is at stake when France and Morocco meet in a highly anticipated quarter-final clash tomorrow morning. France, making their 16th FIFA World Cup appearance, are chasing a third world title after triumphs in 1998 and 2018. The 2018 champions and 2022 runners-up have once again looked like serious title contenders, with a squad packed with attacking quality and tournament experience. France has scored 14 goals on their way to the last eight, with captain Kylian Mbappé leading the attack with seven goals at this year’s tournament.

news.title: ‘Not today, not here’: Infantino tight-lipped on abandoned World Cup rights proposal
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who attended the opening match of the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Katowice on Saturday, remained tight-lipped about whether he regrets his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup. The event is the first tournament organised by world soccer's ruling body since the Swiss administrator called off the plan, which valued the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments at $20 billion. The proposal was abandoned in late July following a fierce backlash and boycott threats from regional governing bodies, including Europe's UEFA and major stakeholders in the sport. news.title: FIFA blasts UEFA ‘smear campaign,’ fights World Cup plan disclosures
news.lede: FIFA has accused UEFA of a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition" after European football's governing body asked US judges to force it to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan. Global soccer body FIFA's divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped. While FIFA quickly aborted the plans in response to the backlash, UEFA is now preparing possible legal action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino for alleged "criminal mismanagement." Last week, it filed requests in three US states requesting the disclosure of documents related to the plan from FIFA and partners, including prospective lead investor Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital firm.
